newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: RESEARCH ALERT - Sri Lanka EPS sharply up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Sri Lanka EPS sharply up in 1997.

text.p: Brokerage Lanka Securities said earnings per share (EPS) growth of Sri Lankan corporates should rise sharply in 1997 because of low interest rates.
"We anticipate an EPS growth rate between 14 and 15 percent in the 1997 financial year, from a mere three percent experienced in 1996," it said in a report seen by Reuters on Wednesday.
The report said growth will be spurred by low interest rates, which would induce calls for credit.
Interest rates have eased this year because of improved money supply after the Central Bank cut reserve ratios by three percent.
The benchmark one-year Treasury Bill yield was at 12.72 at last Wednesday's auction, down from 17.11 percent on January 3.
Banks are seen leading the upswing in EPS growth, the report said.
"Although spreads will erode somewhat during the year, the growth in lending will be strong enough to ensure double digit earnings growth in the banks, finance and insurance sector," it said.
The sector accounts for approximately 29 percent of Colombo stock market capitalisation, which was 129.6 billion rupees on Tuesday. ($1 = 59.3 rupees) --- Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
